FILED s407 (Fable review, fable-answers-s406.md Â§5.4).  Probed vs perl 5.40.3:

    use Math::Trig;                perl        PCL
    print pi, "\n"                 3.14159..   pi          <- bareword string
    my @l = (pi, 1)                3.14.. 1    pi 1
    my $w = 2 * pi                 6.28..      0
    my $z = pi + 1                 4.14..      3.14..      <- parsed as pi(+1): a LIST OP
    my $x = pi / 2                 1.57..      0           (and `pi / 2 + pi / 4` is now a #351
                                                            match repair -> DROP, announced)
  INVERSE (right today):
    my $y = pi                     3.14..      3.14..      <- parse()'s single-element bareword branch
    print foo(pi)                  foo(3.14)   foo(3.14)
    use constant lc_c => 7; lc_c + 1 / print lc_c, "\n"    8 / 7  both right (DECLARED in doc)

So the module's prototypes ARE known to the environment (`my $y = pi` proves
_is_zero_arg_func sees it) â the operator-loop TERM reading of a bareword does
not ask.  Same site family as #356 (`print PI / 2` dropped, `print PI + 1`
filehandle), which #361 fixed for DECLARED ALL-CAPS constants only.  This is the
#266 classifier ("a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE") asked at one
more site: the operator-loop term reading in PExpr â and Option B's _reduce_term
is the blessed home for that region (docs/pexpr-term-parsing-review.md); check
whether phase 2 absorbs it before patching in place.  Also the #351 repair's
residue: an imported lowercase ()-sub before `/` (invisible to the token scan)
gets repaired to a match; with the environment consulted at PExpr time that
statement would still be division IF the repair did not fire â the repair
cannot know; accept unless the classifier can be reached from the repair (it
cannot today: no environment at repair time).
BAR: the table above as perl-oracle rows; the #356 shapes; corpus-diff; if the
change touches PExpr's term reading, the gate-SET rule (both populations).


=== s438c (Opus 5, 2026-08-23) DONE -- but NOT where this task pointed, and the
difference is the finding.

THE TASK'S PREMISE WAS WRONG: "the module's prototypes ARE known to the
environment (`my $y = pi` proves _is_zero_arg_func sees it) -- the operator-loop
TERM reading of a bareword does not ask."  Measured: `_bareword_callable_here`
IS asked (23 times for `pi` in the reported program) and answers `no`, because
`$env->has_prototype('pi')` is FALSE.  `my $y = pi` is right for an unrelated
reason -- a lone Word emits as a call anyway.  The prototype never crossed the
`use`.

WHERE IT ACTUALLY BROKE: `Pl::Parser::_merge_module_prototypes` imported a
module's prototype only when it affected code generation -- a block arg, or a
parameter SLOT (`$`, `\X`, `@`, `%`) -- or when `export_names` listed it.  A
`()` prototype has NO slots, so it rode entirely on the export scan, and that
scan reads literal `qw()` out of the module's `@EXPORT`/`@EXPORT_OK`
statements.  Math::Complex (where `pi` is actually defined; Math::Trig
re-exports it) builds its list from variables:

    my @trig = qw( pi tan â¦ );
    our @EXPORT = (qw( i Re Im â¦ atan2 ), @trig);

so `pi` reaches @EXPORT through @trig and the scan never sees it.  A LOCAL
module with a literal `qw()` export is right today, and so is a two-level
re-export chain -- both probed, which is what isolated the export scan.

THE FIX, one line at the merge plus one shared predicate: an EMPTY prototype is
a PARSE fact (it makes the bareword a TERM), so it crosses a `use` on the same
footing as `has_block_arg`, independent of the export scan.  Following the
variable-built export list instead would mean interpreting the module's own
code; keying on the prototype is the layer rule.

RULE 11 APPLIED: the record test ("min_params 0 and no params") existed in TWO
copies -- PExpr::_is_zero_arg_func and, implicitly, nowhere in the merge, which
is how they disagreed.  It is now ONE predicate,
`Pl::Environment::proto_is_zero_arg`, and both ask it.  (`is_proto` does NOT
distinguish the shape: `sub pi ()` arrives as is_proto 0 -- measured -- because
parse_prototype_or_signature's empty case and `use constant` register it that
way.  A first attempt keyed on `is_proto` and changed nothing.)

MEASURED: the whole #365 table now matches perl row for row (print pi / (pi, 1)
/ 2 * pi / pi + 1 / pi / 2 / foo(pi) / my $y = pi), and the inverses stay right
(`use constant lc_c => 7` gives 8 and 7).  Emission IDENTICAL: corpus-diff 111
files, and emission-ab over lib/**.pm + cpan-tests/** + perl's own t/ = 951
files SAME, 0 DIFF, 0 RCDIFF -- so the wider import moves nothing, and the
over-import risk it carries (a module's non-exported `()` sub becoming callable
in the using file) does not materialise in any measured population.  Gate
165/5760.  Guard `Pl/t/imported-term-01.t`, 7 both_agree rows against live perl
with a fixture module that builds its @EXPORT from a VARIABLE the way
Math::Complex does -- so the row tests the mechanism, not one CPAN module's
spelling; inverse guard on a fe46c7b worktree: rows 1-4 fail, 5-7 pass.

RESIDUE, filed as #484 and pre-existing: `pi / 2 + pi / 4` (TWO slashes) is
still repaired to a match and dropped.  This task guessed the classifier could
not be reached from the #351 repair; it CAN -- `_repair_word_match` already
asks `_word_is_term` -- but that predicate reads only THIS DOCUMENT's terms,
and the prototype pre-merge runs AFTER the repair block.  #484 has both
candidate fixes and says which to measure first.
subject: SILENT WRONG: an IMPORTED ()-prototype sub is a STRING in operator/list positions â `use Math::Trig; print pi, "\n"` prints "pi"; `2 * pi` is 0; `pi + 1` parses as pi(+1)
